nodes.name: Pt loading via ion exchange and calcination
nodes.procedure: The FeOOH@NiFe LDHs (detailed synthesis from ref [39]) were put into a solution containing 0.005 M H₂PtCl₆ (1 mL), soaked at room temperature for 1 h, dried in an oven at 60°C. Subsequently, calcined at 300°C for 2 h in tube furnace (heating rate 5°C/min) under argon atmosphere. The catalyst was labeled Pt/FeOOH@NiFe LDHs.

nodes.source_text: Then, the FeOOH@NiFe LDHs were put into a solution containing 0.005 M H₂PtCl₆ (1 mL), soaked at room temperature for 1 h, and dried in an oven at 60°C. Subsequently, it was calcined at 300°C for 2 h in a tube furnace with a heating rate of 5°C/min under an argon atmosphere.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM and HRTEM show nanoflower-like structure of Pt/FeOOH@NiFe LDHs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pt/FeOOH@NiFe LDHs present a nanoflower-like structure (Figures 1b and S1).

properties.description: High mag nanoflower with markings (10 nm scale)

nodes.characterization_summary: Spherical aberration electron microscopy image shows Pt single atoms (red circles) and Pt clusters (yellow circles) with size 0.5-1.5 nm at amorphous FeOOH area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1d. Apparently, a small amount of Pt exhibits a single-atom distribution, and there are Pt clusters with a size of 0.51.5 nm at the amorphous area of FeOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows Pt diffraction peaks at 40°, 46°, and 67° corresponding to (111), (220), and (220) crystal planes of Pt; no extra NiFe LDHs diffraction peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD characterization in Figure 2a confirmed the presence of Pt in Pt/FeOOH@NiFe LDHs, and 40°, 46°, and 67° diffraction peaks correspond to the (111), (220), and (220) crystal planes of Pt.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman peaks of Pt/FeOOH@NiFe LDHs shifted to lower wavenumbers compared to NiFe LDHs and FeOOH@NiFe LDHs due to more structural defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2b, NiFe LDHs and FeOOH@NiFe LDHs have typical NiO characteristic peaks at 531.8 cm^{-1}. The Raman peaks of Pt/FeOOH@NiFe LDHs shifted to lower wavenumbers because more structural defects were formed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f shows Pt^0 (70.82, 74.18 eV, 44.8%) and Pt^{2+} (72.55, 75.91 eV, 55.2%); Ni 2p positively shifted 0.4 eV; Fe^{3+} content increased to 70.6%; indicates strong Pt-FeOOH electronic interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pt 4f spectrum in Figure 2c confirmed the presence of Pt^0 at binding energies of 70.82 and 74.18 eV and Pt^{2+} at binding energies of 72.55 and 75.91 eV with a similar content (44.8 vs. 55.2%) in Pt/FeOOH@NiFe LDHs.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge: valence ~+3, coordination Fe-O 4.1, Fe-M 2.8; Pt L3-edge: average valence +0.14, Pt-O 0.8, Pt-Pt 1.0 confirming Pt single-atom/cluster coexistence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EXAFS fitting in Table S1 confirmed that each Fe atom coordinates with 4.1 oxygen atoms and 2.8 nearby metals in Pt/FeOOH@NiFe LDHs... the coordination numbers of Pt-O and Pt-Pt are 0.8 and 1.0, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV gives C_dl = 26 mF cm^{-2} for ECSA calculation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Pt/FeOOH@NiFe LDHs have a higher C_dl value of 26 mF cm^{-2}

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows smallest semicircle indicating lowest charge-transfer resistance R_ct among compared catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 4f, the Nyquist plot of Pt/FeOOH@NiFe LDHs shows that the semicircle is the smallest in these catalysts, indicating the lowest charge-transfer resistance (R_ct).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows Pt content of 2 wt% in Pt/FeOOH@NiFe LDHs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry result, the weight percentage of Pt in Pt/FeOOH@NiFe LDHs is 2 wt %.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, Pt, and O elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni, Fe, Pt, and O are uniformly distributed, which can be confirmed by the energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping images (Figures 1e-i and S3).
